title: Campaign Comparison (golden batch)
description: Overlay the current campaign against a reference ('golden') run by shifting the reference in time. Use to answer 'is this run behaving like the good one?' — the question a live trend cannot answer.

list.name: offset
list.label: Reference offset
list.description: How far back the reference campaign sits. The reference series is shifted forward by this amount so both runs line up on the same axis.
list.query: 1 day,7 days,14 days,30 days,90 days,180 days,365 days

list.name: tag
list.label: Tag
list.query: SELECT name AS __text, id AS __value FROM tag_definition ORDER BY name

options.content:
Solid = **current** window. Dashed/suffixed `(ref)` = the same window shifted back by **$offset**. Divergence between the two is the signal; absolute values are secondary.

Both series come from `tag_sample_1m`, so this works back to two years. Beyond that, switch the queries to `tag_sample_1h`.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('$__interval', a.bucket) AS time,
       t.name                                AS metric,
       sum(a.sum_value) / NULLIF(sum(a.sample_count), 0) AS value
FROM tag_sample_1m a
JOIN tag_definition t ON t.id = a.tag_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(a.bucket)
  AND a.tag_id IN ($tag)
GROUP BY 1, 2

UNION ALL

-- Reference run, shifted forward so it overlays the current window.
SELECT time_bucket('$__interval', a.bucket + INTERVAL '$offset') AS time,
       t.name || ' (ref)'                                        AS metric,
       sum(a.sum_value) / NULLIF(sum(a.sample_count), 0)         AS value
FROM tag_sample_1m a
JOIN tag_definition t ON t.id = a.tag_id
WHERE a.bucket BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - INTERVAL '$offset'
                   AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz   - INTERVAL '$offset'
  AND a.tag_id IN ($tag)
GROUP BY 1, 2

ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Campaign statistics — current vs reference
panels.description: Whole-window summary. A shifted mean with an unchanged min/max usually indicates a setpoint change; a widened min/max with an unchanged mean usually indicates degraded control.

targets.rawSql:
WITH current_window AS (
  SELECT a.tag_id,
         sum(a.sum_value) / NULLIF(sum(a.sample_count), 0) AS mean,
         min(a.min_value) AS lo,
         max(a.max_value) AS hi
  FROM tag_sample_1m a
  WHERE $__timeFilter(a.bucket) AND a.tag_id IN ($tag)
  GROUP BY a.tag_id
),
reference AS (
  SELECT a.tag_id,
         sum(a.sum_value) / NULLIF(sum(a.sample_count), 0) AS mean,
         min(a.min_value) AS lo,
         max(a.max_value) AS hi
  FROM tag_sample_1m a
  WHERE a.bucket BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - INTERVAL '$offset'
                     AND $__timeTo()::timestamptz   - INTERVAL '$offset'
    AND a.tag_id IN ($tag)
  GROUP BY a.tag_id
)
SELECT t.name                                    AS "Tag",
       round(c.mean::numeric, 3)                 AS "Mean (now)",
       round(r.mean::numeric, 3)                 AS "Mean (ref)",
       round((c.mean - r.mean)::numeric, 3)      AS "Delta",
       round(c.lo::numeric, 3)                   AS "Min (now)",
       round(c.hi::numeric, 3)                   AS "Max (now)",
       round(r.lo::numeric, 3)                   AS "Min (ref)",
       round(r.hi::numeric, 3)                   AS "Max (ref)"
FROM current_window c
FULL OUTER JOIN reference r ON r.tag_id = c.tag_id
JOIN tag_definition t ON t.id = COALESCE(c.tag_id, r.tag_id)
ORDER BY t.name
